proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Virchow2 (Prism slide embedding) is the strongest single model (0.860 AUROC, lowest fold SD); UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 are ~0.82-0.83. Adding metadata slightly hurts every model, so age/sex carries little signal beyond the image embeddings.
REASONING: Start with the simplest robust fusion as an anchor. Use late fusion with mean_prob, which needs no inner-CV weight learning and so has low variance with 134 training patients. Use moderate regularisation (C=0.01) with L2 normalisation and standardisation, no PCA, and meta_weight 1. This maps whether simple averaging of the three models beats Virchow2 alone.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.86-0.87, i.e. at or slightly above Virchow2. If it falls below 0.85, averaging dilutes Virchow2 with the weaker models. In that case weighted combinations (learned_weights or stack) or early fusion with balance_blocks become the priority.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion with mean_prob (C=0.01, L2) reaches 0.849, below virchow2 alone (0.860). Averaging appears to dilute the stronger Virchow2 signal with the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 models. Metadata does not help any single model.
REASONING: This is still the exploration phase, so map the early-fusion method next. Settings: concatenation with balance_blocks=True so no model dominates by width, PCA 64 per model to cut dimensionality for 134 training patients, L2 norm, and moderate regularisation C=0.01. This tests whether a joint linear model can exploit complementary features that probability averaging cannot.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.85-0.87. If it stays below 0.86, the weaker models add noise rather than complementary signal under joint fitting. In that case the most plausible remaining route is late fusion with learned_weights or stack, which can upweight Virchow2.

ANALYSIS: Both fusions (late mean_prob 0.849, early PCA64 0.847) fall below the best single model, virchow2 at 0.860. Weaker UNI2/H-optimus members likely dilute Virchow2 under equal-weight combining. Adding metadata slightly hurt every single model, so meta_weight=1 is fine and higher values are unlikely to help.
REASONING: Learned simplex weights from inner CV could upweight Virchow2 and recover at least single-model performance. That would test whether fusion can add complementary signal. It also maps an untested combine mode during exploration. I keep the other knobs equal to trial #1 so the comparison is paired and clean.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.855-0.865, with weights concentrated on Virchow2. If it stays around 0.85, the inner-CV weights are too noisy with 134 patients, and fixed weighting or stacking with strong regularisation should be explored next. Alternatively, C may be mis-set, so a C sweep is the other follow-up.

ANALYSIS: Both fusions so far (late mean_prob 0.849, early PCA64 0.847) fall short of Virchow2 alone (0.860). Learned_weights edged up (+0.004, n.s.), probably by upweighting Virchow2. Equal-weight fusion seems to dilute the strongest model. Papillary (0.74) and Lepidic (0.77) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: We are still exploring and the gated method is untested. A per-patient gate could learn to lean on Virchow2 while still drawing on the others for hard classes. I am using strong regularisation (PCA64 per model, hidden 32, dropout 0.5, wd 0.1, 200 epochs, lr 1e-3, 3 seeds) because each fold has only 134 training patients.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.84-0.86. If it clearly beats 0.849, gated is worth tuning. If it comes in at or below the late baselines with higher fold SD, the method is overfitting or too noisy for this data size. I would then drop it and focus on late fusion (stacking, different C) or early fusion without balance_blocks, so Virchow2's larger block gets more weight.

ANALYSIS: All three fusion families (late mean_prob 0.849, early 0.847, gated 0.845) land below the Virchow2-only baseline (0.860). Equal-weight fusion seems to dilute the strongest model. Learned simplex weights recovered a little (+0.0036), which fits the idea that Virchow2 needs more weight. Lepidic and Papillary (~0.74-0.78) are the weak classes in every method.
REASONING: Stacking is the main untested combiner. A second logistic regression on per-model log-probabilities can learn class-specific reliance on each model, for example Virchow2 for Papillary/Lepidic and the others where they help. That is more flexible than one global simplex weight. I keep every other knob as in #1 so the effect is isolated to the combiner. stack_C=0.1 is moderate regularisation, chosen for the roughly 134-patient inner-CV meta-training set.
EXPECTED: If class-specific weighting matters, AUROC should rise to about 0.855-0.865 with gains in Papillary/Lepidic, possibly clearing the threshold. If it scores at or below 0.85, the meta-learner is too noisy at this sample size. In that case I would conclude the bottleneck is base-model regularisation (C, PCA), not the combiner, and explore C next.

ANALYSIS: No fusion beats single Virchow2 (0.860). Late, early, gated and stack all land at 0.845-0.853 with similar per-class profiles, so the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 seem to dilute Virchow2. The regularisation strength C has only been tested at 0.01, and full-dimensional early fusion has not been tried.
REASONING: Use the exploration budget on the knob most likely to matter: regularisation scale under early fusion with full features (no PCA). With balance_blocks, each 1536- or 2560-d block is scaled by about 1/39-1/50, which makes the effective penalty very strong. A larger C (1.0) is therefore needed to test whether the weaker-regularisation regime lets the classifier exploit complementary signal that PCA-64 may discard.
EXPECTED: If PCA or over-shrinkage was limiting early fusion, AUROC should rise to about 0.86 or higher, with gains in Papillary and Lepidic. If it stays at about 0.85, compression and C are not the bottleneck. I would then try Virchow2-weighted approaches (learned weights or stack with different C) or accept that fusion adds little beyond Virchow2.

ANALYSIS: No fusion beats Virchow2 alone (0.860). Every fusion lands at 0.845-0.853, so combining models seems to dilute the strongest model rather than add to it. Weaker regularisation hurt early fusion (C=1 gave 0.834 vs 0.847 at C=0.01). Learned weights and stacking gave small gains that did not reach the threshold.
REASONING: This is an exploration trial, so it is worth answering two open questions at once: does stronger L2 shrinkage help in the high-dimensional concatenation, and does letting blocks scale by their size (Virchow2 has 2560 columns versus 1536 for each of the others) help. Early fusion without balance_blocks gives the best model more columns, and C=0.001 tests the low-C direction that the C=1 result points toward. PCA is left off to keep all of the Virchow2 signal.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.855-0.865, which could approach or beat the Virchow2 baseline and clear the threshold over trial #1. If it stays at or below 0.85, I will conclude that early concatenation saturates at this level regardless of block weighting or regularisation. In that case I will turn to late fusion at lower C or a different meta_weight.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion improves as regularisation gets stronger: C=1 gave 0.834, C=0.01 with PCA64 gave 0.847, and C=0.001 on full features gave 0.859 (accepted). The best fusion still only matches Virchow2 alone (0.860), so it has not yet beaten the single-model baseline. Late, stack and gated fusion all sit around 0.845-0.853. Papillary (~0.74) and Lepidic (~0.77) are the weak classes in every method.
REASONING: The clearest signal so far is that stronger shrinkage helps. Trying C=0.0001 tests whether that trend keeps going. At such strong shrinkage the model behaves almost like a class-centroid classifier, which often suits very high-dimensional data with only 134 patients per fold. All other knobs stay as in #7, so any change can be attributed to C. This is still the exploration phase, so mapping this boundary costs nothing toward the stop rule.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.86-0.87, with a possible gain on Papillary and Lepidic. If it drops below #7, then C=0.001 is near the optimum. In that case I would next vary l2_normalize, balance_blocks or meta_weight at C=0.001 rather than push regularisation further.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far ties with Virchow2 alone (0.860). The best fused result is early concat with strong regularization (C=0.001 or 0.0001, about 0.86); weaker regularization (C=1) clearly hurts. Late fusion was only tried at C=0.01, where learned_weights and stack were slightly better than mean_prob. Per-class weak spots are Papillary (~0.75) and Lepidic (~0.77).
REASONING: Strong shrinkage helped early fusion, so the late base models were likely under-regularized at C=0.01. Combining stronger-regularized per-model classifiers with learned simplex weights lets the combiner upweight Virchow2 while still borrowing complementary signal from UNI2-h and H-optimus. This is the most plausible untested route to a clear gain over trial #7, and it maps the C axis for late fusion during exploration.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.865-0.870 with lower fold SD than trial #7. If it stays near 0.855-0.86, the late-fusion C axis is not the bottleneck, and the next step is to test l2_normalize=False or PCA inside early fusion.

ANALYSIS: All fusions land at about 0.85-0.86 AUROC, which is no clear gain over Virchow2 alone (0.860). In early fusion, stronger shrinkage helped: C=1 gave 0.834, C=0.01 with PCA and balanced blocks gave 0.847, and C=0.001 gave 0.859 (accepted). C=0.0001 added nothing beyond that. Unbalanced blocks let the 2560-d Virchow2 block dominate, which may explain why it does well. Late learned_weights reaches the same level. Gated fusion is no better. Metadata adds little or even hurts. Per-slide L2 normalisation has been on in every trial, so its effect is untested.
REASONING: This is the last exploration trial, so it should settle an open knob rather than repeat a tested setting. l2_normalize=False is the main untested common knob. The Prism2 Virchow2 slide embedding and the mean-pooled tile embeddings may carry useful information in their norms (for example tissue composition or density), and per-slide L2 normalisation would erase it. The trial keeps everything else equal to the best config (early, C=0.001, no PCA, unbalanced blocks), so the comparison is clean.
EXPECTED: Most likely a small change of about ±0.005. If AUROC rises clearly (by 0.01 or more), the norm carries signal and later trials should switch to l2_normalize=False. If it drops or stays flat, keep L2 normalisation and focus on block weighting, e.g. late fusion with mean_logit at C=0.001, or meta_weight. A flat result would also strengthen the view that fusion is capped near Virchow2's performance.

ANALYSIS: Strong L2 shrinkage is the one knob with a clear effect. Early fusion at C=0.001 (#7) was accepted, and late learned_weights also improved when C went from 0.01 to 0.001 (0.8525 to 0.8606). Even so, every fusion so far sits at about 0.86, which matches virchow2 alone. Combine rules, L2 norm and C below 0.001 changed nothing beyond noise. Stacking (#5) had the lowest fold SD and the best Lepidic AUROC (0.83), but its base models were under-regularised (C=0.01).
REASONING: This trial pairs the best base regularisation (C=0.001) with stacking, the only combiner that showed a qualitatively different per-class profile. The meta-learner can weight each model per class, for example leaning on other models for Lepidic and Cribriform where Virchow2 may be weaker. That is the most plausible route to a gain above noise rather than another tweak to the C grid. stack_C=0.01 keeps the 21+2-feature meta-learner heavily regularised given only about 134 patients per fold.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.865-0.875 with a low fold SD and Lepidic near 0.83 while Papillary holds. If the gain over #7 stays under the threshold, per-class weighting of the models adds nothing beyond simple averaging. In that case the three embeddings are largely redundant for this task, and I would next test PCA-reduced early fusion as a final check before concluding that fusion does not beat Virchow2.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion family lands near 0.85–0.86 AUROC, which is roughly Virchow2 alone (0.860). Strong shrinkage clearly helps early fusion: C=1 gave 0.834, C=0.01 with balanced PCA64 gave 0.847, and C=0.001–0.0001 gave about 0.860. Unbalanced blocks, which let Virchow2's 2560 columns dominate, did best. Late combiners (learned_weights, stack) all plateau at about 0.86, with gains far below the threshold. Papillary (about 0.75) and Lepidic (about 0.77) are the weak classes.
REASONING: The open question for early fusion is whether reducing dimension per model helps, rather than shrinking 5600 raw dimensions heavily. Compressing each model to its top 32 directions keeps the main morphology axes, cuts the noise dimensions, and makes block sizes equal. A moderate C=0.01 can then fit those axes more sharply than the heavy shrinkage C=0.001 needs on raw features. Trial #2 used PCA64 with balance_blocks=True, so the effects of PCA and balancing were confounded. This trial uses unbalanced blocks with smaller PCA, testing PCA dimension and C on a different axis than earlier trials.
EXPECTED: Expected AUROC is about 0.86–0.87, possibly with better Papillary and Lepidic AUROC. If it does not beat #7 by more than the threshold, I will conclude that PCA gives no benefit over strong L2 shrinkage. In that case the fusion ceiling is probably set by the information in Virchow2, and remaining trials should target meta_weight or a strongly regularised gated model rather than PCA settings.

ANALYSIS: Strongly regularised early fusion (L2 norm, no PCA, C=0.001, unbalanced blocks) is the accepted best at 0.8594. It only ties Virchow2 alone (0.8601). Weaker regularisation, PCA and block balancing all hurt. Balancing likely hurts because it shrinks Virchow2's larger block, which seems to carry most of the signal. Late variants at C=0.001 (learned_weights, stack) reach about 0.8605, but their per-fold variance is high. The stack combiner, which re-adds age/sex in the second stage, consistently lifts Lepidic (0.82-0.83 vs 0.77).
REASONING: The Lepidic gain under stacking hints that metadata is being over-shrunk in the heavily regularised early model. At C=0.001 the 2 age/sex columns are penalised as hard as about 7600 image features. meta_weight is the only common knob not yet tested. Raising it to 3 isolates this question on the current best configuration at negligible cost.
EXPECTED: Lepidic and possibly In situ AUROC should rise to about 0.80+, for a macro gain of about 0.005-0.01 that might clear the threshold. If Lepidic does not move, the stacking gain came from the probability recombination, not from metadata. Then meta_weight=10 is not worth trying, and I would next probe late mean_logit or C=0.0001 late fusion.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far lands at about 0.855-0.861 AUROC, which is no better than Virchow2 alone (0.860). Strong shrinkage helps both early and late fusion: C=0.001 beats 0.01, which beats 1.0. PCA (32/64) and balance_blocks hurt, and age/sex add nothing. Late fusion with learned_weights or stack ties early fusion. The only gated trial (#4) was weakly regularised and got 0.845, so gated is still the least explored method.
REASONING: Retuning early or late fusion is unlikely to clear the acceptance threshold of about 0.006-0.015, because those trials keep landing within ±0.002 of the best. Gated fusion is the one mechanism that can weight models per patient, which could help the weak classes (Papillary 0.76, Lepidic 0.77). Its first trial overfit, so I am trying it with heavy regularisation: hidden=16, dropout 0.5, weight_decay 1.0 and 100 epochs. I keep more signal with PCA 128, since lower PCA dimensions hurt the linear models.
EXPECTED: If per-patient gating helps, AUROC should be at least 0.865 with better Papillary and Lepidic AUROC. If it stays at or below about 0.855, I will conclude the gate cannot be learned from 134 patients per fold. I would then accept that the fusion ceiling is about the Virchow2 level and spend only a few cheap checks, such as late fusion with mean_logit at C=0.001, before letting the stop rule end the search.

ANALYSIS: Strong regularisation drives everything: early fusion at C≤0.001 without PCA (#7, #8) and late fusion at C=0.001 (#9, #11) all reach about 0.860. That equals Virchow2 alone (0.8601), so fusion has not yet added real signal. PCA, balance_blocks, larger C and gated networks all hurt. Lepidic and Papillary remain the weakest classes; stacking lifted Lepidic but lost elsewhere.
REASONING: mean_logit is the one late combiner not yet tested at the good regularisation level (C=0.001). A geometric mean of the per-model probabilities sharpens agreement between models. It needs no inner-CV fitting, so it avoids the variance that inflated the thresholds for learned_weights and stack. This answers the open question of whether a low-variance late combine can beat early concatenation at the same C.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.860-0.866, with lower fold SD than #7. Acceptance needs a gain of about 0.01 over #7, which a fusion that only matches Virchow2 cannot deliver. If it lands near 0.860 or is rejected, I will conclude that, under this regularisation, the three models carry largely redundant information beyond Virchow2. The remaining budget would then go to a few targeted checks (e.g. meta_weight=10, a late stack variant) before letting the stop rule end the search.

ANALYSIS: Fusion plateaus around 0.860 AUROC, essentially tied with Virchow2 alone (0.8601). Strong L2 regularisation (C≤0.001) is the one knob that clearly helped, for both early and late fusion. PCA, balance_blocks, gating and a higher meta_weight were neutral or harmful. Among combiners, mean_logit gave the best balanced accuracy (0.506), but no combiner gave an AUROC gain that cleared the threshold.
REASONING: Late fusion with the C=0.0001 base models is untested. In early fusion, moving from C=0.001 to C=0.0001 lowered the fold SD (0.031 to 0.026), so stronger shrinkage may stabilise the per-model base learners. A geometric mean of logits then pools three weak but stable experts. This is the cheapest remaining test of whether late fusion can beat early fusion at the regularisation optimum. Balanced blocks are avoided because they down-weight Virchow2, the strongest model.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.861 to 0.865 with a lower fold SD. A clear gain is plausible but uncertain. If the gain stays below the threshold, I will conclude the space is saturated near the Virchow2 ceiling: fusion adds stability and balanced accuracy but not AUROC. Remaining trials should then probe only a few untried directions (e.g. late stack at very low stack_C, or early with pca=128).

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.860 AUROC (best is #7, early, C=0.001, L2 norm, no PCA, 0.8594). This matches Virchow2 alone (0.8601), so no fusion has yet clearly beaten the best single model. Strong regularisation (C=0.001) is the main lever. PCA, block balancing, extra metadata weight and the gated model all hurt or were neutral. Among the late combiners, stacking is the only one with a distinct per-class profile: Lepidic reached 0.82-0.83 against 0.77-0.78 elsewhere, with lower fold SD. That hints at per-class complementarity between the models that the simple averages wash out.
REASONING: The stacker at stack_C=0.01 (#11) is heavily shrunk, so it can barely learn class-specific model weights. Relaxing it to stack_C=0.1 on the well-regularised base models (C=0.001) is the untested combination most likely to use per-class complementarity. For example, it could combine the Lepidic gain with the better Papillary and Micropapillary scores of the mean combiners. Other untested directions (PCA 128, meta_weight 10, weighted_vote) have little prior support from the log.
EXPECTED: I expect Lepidic around 0.82 with Micropapillary and Papillary held near 0.88 and 0.76, giving roughly 0.865-0.87 macro AUROC. If it lands at about 0.86 or below, or fails the stack's high threshold, I will conclude that per-class stacking adds no robust signal at n=134 per fold. I would then treat about 0.86 as the ceiling set by Virchow2, and spend at most a couple more trials (for example one gated variant without PCA) before letting the stop rule end the search.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at the Virchow2-alone level, about 0.860. Early at C=0.001 with L2 normalisation and no PCA (#7) is the accepted best. Late variants at C=0.001 (learned_weights, mean_logit, stack) are all within ±0.001 of it. PCA consistently hurt early fusion (pca=32/64 lost about 0.014). Both gated trials used PCA (64 or 128) and scored 0.842-0.845.
REASONING: The linear fusions are clearly saturated, so another C or combine tweak would only chase noise. The open question is whether gated lost because of the PCA bottleneck rather than the gating itself, since PCA was the knob that hurt early fusion. Running gated on the full L2-normalised embeddings tests this directly. It keeps the regularisation from #4 (dropout 0.5, weight_decay 0.1, 200 epochs) and uses a moderate hidden size of 64.
EXPECTED: If PCA was the limit, gated should rise to about 0.86 or higher, and a per-patient gate might improve Lepidic and Papillary, the weakest classes. If it stays at 0.845 or below, I will conclude gated fusion overfits at n=134 and drop it. The remaining budget would then go to a few targeted early/late checks, accepting that fusion roughly matches Virchow2 alone.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion family has plateaued at about 0.86 AUROC, which equals Virchow2 alone (0.8601). The accepted best, early fusion with L2 norm, no PCA and C=0.001 (#7), only beat the weak first late trial. PCA (32/64) and very high C hurt, meta_weight has no effect, and gated networks overfit. Late combiners (mean_logit, learned_weights, stack) all tie at about 0.860, within noise.
REASONING: One structural question is still open: does balance_blocks help at a well-tuned regularisation? It has only been tested with PCA64 at C=0.01 and at C=1 (#6, where the effective regularisation was weaker). Block scaling of about 1/sqrt(1500-2560) shrinks each block's effective C by about 1/1500-1/2560. So C=0.1 with balancing roughly matches the strength of the best unbalanced setting (C≈0.0001-0.001), while shifting relative weight toward UNI2-h and H-optimus. This isolates the effect of the inter-model weighting from the regularisation strength.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC 0.850-0.860, rejected. That would mean letting Virchow2 dominate through its larger block is better, and that the other models add little beyond Virchow2. A clear gain (>0.866) would mean the complementary UNI2-h/H-optimus signal is being under-used, and I would then refine C around 0.01-1 with balancing. If it fails, the remaining budget should go to a few decisive checks, such as weighted_vote, rather than tuning noise.

ANALYSIS: Every reasonable fusion lands near 0.855-0.861. That is the same as Virchow2 alone (0.860), so the other two models add little beyond Virchow2. The best is early fusion with L2 normalisation, no PCA and strong shrinkage (C=0.001 to 0.0001). Over-weak regularisation, PCA at 32 or 64, and the gated net all hurt. Late combiners (learned_weights, stack, mean_logit) give gains of +0.001 or less, well below the thresholds.
REASONING: Block balancing has only been tried at C of 1 or below. Balancing shrinks each image column by 1/sqrt(d), so its effective regularisation is about C/d. At C=1 that is roughly 0.0004-0.0007, near the best range, yet the run scored 0.834. It also left age/sex comparatively unshrunk. C=10 gives image blocks an effective C of about 0.004-0.0065, between the two best unbalanced settings. This tests whether equal model weighting helps once regularisation is matched, which is the main untested structural question for early fusion. The alternatives are near-duplicates: PCA at 128 is close to full rank with 134 patients, and other late combiners have plateaued.
EXPECTED: Most likely about 0.85-0.86, not accepted. A clear gain (>0.01), especially on Papillary and Lepidic, would show that Virchow2's 2560 dimensions dominate the unbalanced concatenation. If it fails, I conclude the fusion ceiling is Virchow2-level. I would then spend the few remaining trials on low-risk checks such as late weighted_vote, and otherwise let the stop rule end the search.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.859–0.861 AUROC (early C=0.001 is the accepted best at 0.8594). That is no better than Virchow2 alone (0.8601). Strong L2 regularisation (C≤0.001) and no block balancing work best. PCA, balance_blocks, weak regularisation and gated fusion all hurt, and gated overfits as expected. Stacking gives the best Lepidic (0.81–0.83) and Papillary (0.77) AUROCs, but its fold variance makes the threshold large (0.016–0.02).
REASONING: Few open questions could still give a clear gain. The stacker's per-class flexibility is the only mechanism that has shifted per-class AUROCs, lifting Lepidic by about 0.05. Its noise appears to come from fitting a 21+2-feature meta-model on inner-CV predictions with little shrinkage. stack_C=0.001 is untested. Combined with the good base C=0.001, it should keep the class-specific gains while cutting the variance that inflates the acceptance threshold. Weighted_vote is also untested, but votes discard ranking information, so it is unlikely to help AUROC.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.862–0.868 with a lower fold SD than #11/#17, keeping Lepidic near 0.82 and Micropapillary near 0.88. If it again lands around 0.86 or is rejected, I will conclude the combination method does not matter here and the fused signal is capped by Virchow2. The remaining trials would then add little, and stopping is acceptable.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion family has plateaued at about 0.86 AUROC, roughly equal to Virchow2 alone (0.8601). Unbalanced early fusion with strong shrinkage (C=0.001 to 0.0001) and late combiners at C=0.001 (learned_weights, mean_logit, stack) all land between 0.859 and 0.861. PCA, balance_blocks, extra meta_weight and gated networks all hurt. balance_blocks probably hurts because it down-weights the larger, strongest Virchow2 block.
REASONING: One clear gap remains in the C curve for the accepted early-fusion family: unbalanced, no PCA, C=0.01. That setting lies between the plateau at C≤0.001 and the drops seen at higher C, which so far were only measured with balance_blocks=True. A modestly weaker penalty may let the strong Virchow2 features contribute more without the block down-weighting. This is the cheapest remaining question that could plausibly move the score.
EXPECTED: Most likely an AUROC of about 0.855 to 0.862, which would be rejected. If it is clearly lower (below 0.85), the regularization optimum is confirmed at C≤0.001. That would mean fusion offers no detectable gain over Virchow2 on this data, and the remaining non-improving trials should be spent only on genuinely new questions rather than retuning.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at Virchow2-alone level (~0.860). The accepted best, early fusion with L2 and C=0.001 (#7), equals the best single model, and late, stack and gated variants all land between 0.84 and 0.86. Strong regularization (C≈0.001) is the one knob that clearly helps. PCA, high C and gated nets hurt. Balance_blocks was only ever tested at C≥0.01, where it never helped.
REASONING: With 3 non-improving trials left, the cleanest untested question is whether block balancing helps in the strongly regularized regime that works. At C=0.01, balanced (#2, with PCA 64) and unbalanced (#22) scored about the same, so the C=0.001 comparison is open. Balancing changes the relative shrinkage of UNI2-h, H-optimus-1 and Virchow2, and with heavier regularization it could let the weaker models add complementary signal (for example Papillary and Lepidic) without swamping the strongest model.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC around 0.85-0.86, with no accepted gain. A gain above about 0.008 would mean balanced, heavily shrunk fusion extracts real complementarity. If it fails, I conclude that Virchow2 alone captures nearly all the signal. Fusion of these slide embeddings then gives no measurable benefit on 167 patients, and the search should stop rather than chase noise.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.860 AUROC, which is the same as Virchow2 alone (0.8601). Strong shrinkage was the only knob that clearly helped (C=0.001 in early and late fusion). L2 norm, block balancing, meta_weight and the late combiner each moved results by less than the noise threshold. Moderate PCA (32 or 64) hurt or did nothing. Gated fusion overfits more as capacity rises; Lepidic AUROC collapses first (0.60 with hidden=64).
REASONING: With 2 trials left before the stop rule, re-tuning the linear methods would only chase sub-threshold differences. The one region not yet mapped is a heavily regularised gated model on low-dimensional inputs: PCA 32, hidden 16, weight decay 1.0, 100 epochs. That gives very little capacity, which matches the evidence that shrinkage is what helps. A per-patient gate is also the only mechanism that could exploit complementarity, for example the gains in Lepidic and Cribriform seen in some fusions. Dropout 0.25 rather than 0.5, because the inputs are already compressed.
EXPECTED: The most likely result is about 0.85-0.86, not accepted. Acceptance needs a gain above roughly 0.01-0.015 with Lepidic and Papillary held up. If it fails, I conclude that on 134 training patients per fold no fusion clearly beats Virchow2's slide embedding, so the best single model (or the accepted early C=0.001 fusion as an equivalent) should go forward, rather than selecting on noise.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.860 AUROC (#7 early C=0.001, #8, #9, #11, #15), which is no better than Virchow2 alone (0.8601). Strong shrinkage (C=0.001) is the only knob that clearly helped. PCA at 32/64 hurt at C=0.01, and so did gating, block balancing at high C, metadata up-weighting and very low stack_C. Per-class gains (Cribriform, Lepidic with stacking) are small and offset by losses elsewhere.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule fires, so it should test an untried knob that could plausibly reduce variance. PCA has only been tested at 32/64 and with weaker shrinkage (C=0.01). Per-model PCA at 128 keeps most of the signal and strips each model's noisy tail dimensions. Combined with the best shrinkage (C=0.001), it could lower fold variance enough to clear the small threshold that applies when trials are highly correlated with #7.
EXPECTED: Most likely the AUROC lands near 0.86, so the gain falls below threshold and the search stops. A clear gain (>~0.006) would show that tail-dimension noise was what limited early fusion. If it does not happen, I conclude that with 167 patients, fusing these embeddings adds nothing measurable over the Virchow2/Prism2 slide embedding. The honest final recommendation is then the simplest strong option: #7, or Virchow2 alone.
